ety.text: Inherited from Old East Slavic -ити (-iti), from Proto-Slavic *-iti. Originally, from Middle Russian, its second person singular form (-ишь (-išʹ)) was always stressed, but in modern Russian is usually non-stressed in transitive verbs. Some exceptions are прости́шь (prostíšʹ), роди́шь (rodíšʹ), сохрани́шь (soxraníšʹ) etc., especially transitional verbs of Old Church Slavonic origin. This change happened mostly around 1600-1700-s, especially in Pskov, Oryol and Smolensk area, under influence from Belarus and Ukraine, where this process has started somewhat earlier.
